Subject: High p99 latency + 502s to /v1/generate since 08/07 (prod)

Folks —

We're seeing elevated p95/p99 latency and intermittent 502/504 errors from our production traffic that hits Redwood's hosted endpoint (api.redwood-prod.example.com). The spike started around the evening of 2026-08-07 and has persisted with intermittent recovery windows. Impact: slowed user sessions and ~12% error rate on generate calls for a handful of critical customers.

What we've captured so far:
- Sample traces show p99 from our region jumping to 1.8–2.5s (normal ~0.4s) and occasional 502 responses.
- Traceroutes indicate a change in egress hop sequence; some flows traverse a third-party proxy cluster before reaching Redwood.
- DNS lookups for api.redwood-prod.example.com intermittently resolve to two different A records; one path correlates with higher loss.

Attached: traceroute output and a short packet summary from our edge. Happy to get on a bridge — this is causing customer tickets to escalate. Please advise next steps and whether you can open an urgent network investigation.

— Ed

On Sun, Aug 9, 2026 at 6:04 PM Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Immediate steps from Redwood: ...

Quick update from our side after a first-pass:
- We see egress path churn originating in a subset of our US-east peering fabric. Multiple flows from Greenline's IP blocks show transient forwarding to a partner proxy cluster (not our owned infra) before entering our colo. When that proxy path is used, we observe increased RTT and higher application-level error rates (502/504).
- DNS: greenline traces show that api.redwood-prod.example.com sometimes resolves to an IP hosted in a different AS that routes via that proxy. We're correlating DNS TTLs and our public A-records to ensure no stale records at recursive resolvers.
- Firewall/proxy: our edge WAF logs show occasional 502s tied to upstream connection resets when the proxy is in-path.

Temporary mitigation options we can enact quickly (need Greenline OK):
1) Pin Greenline traffic to an alternate regional endpoint (us-west-2) for a controlled subset of routes to see if errors abate.
2) Apply an egress bypass rule for Greenline's ASN on our peering fabric (requires network ops change and provider coordination).
3) We can request Greenline re-point DNS to a specific IP while we investigate resolver behavior — note that will cause cache TTL churn on their side.

Attachments: traceroute correlation summary (attached).

If Greenline approves, we'll open a provider support ticket to escalate the partner proxy operator and request packet captures on their hop.

— Sean Gallagher
Sr. Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
